rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment 566fbcc67c564aef84fe850cbd96e80b (CheckRun 5627b36f50384d14851e4b5da991fa96, exit 0, 32 events). Its setup event 30 records the configuration in force containing the late joiner while the restarted node's recovered configuration does not, and its result event 31 records the configuration restored together with the node's snapshot index jumping from 12 to 99 while its last log index stayed at its pre-shutdown value. The installed-snapshot repair path is therefore measured rather than derived, so the parent account is restated with that repair and its limitation replaced; the investigation's discriminator moves to the store variants that remain unmeasured.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled a restarted node does not load the committed configuration entries at or below the commit index it recovers, and both repair paths that bound the consequence are now measured. Gap: restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index, applies the recovered range through processLogs (which ends with setLastApplied), and the scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so a configuration entry at or below that index never reaches processConfigurationLogEntry. Receipt 5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 states both shapes: without a snapshot the node comes back with an empty configuration while its log records the bootstrapped voter, and with a snapshot it comes back holding the snapshot's configuration while the logged configuration change is missing; e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9 reproduces both with the same values. Repair by an arriving configuration entry: in 183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f the node starts with an empty configuration and, after the leader commits one new configuration entry, holds the full set in force. Repair by an installed snapshot: in 5627b36f50384d14851e4b5da991fa96 the node restarts with the snapshot's three-server configuration while the configuration in force already contains a late joiner, the leader has compacted its log past that node's last index, and the node ends with the configuration in force while its snapshot index jumps from 12 to 99 and its last log index stays at its pre-shutdown value, which shows the restoration arrived with a snapshot rather than by log replication. Consequences that remain source-derived rather than measured: runFollower refuses to campaign with no known peers, and quorumSize over an empty or stale voter list is wrong; the child questions measure what the wrong configuration admits and rejects, and what it commits.
counterevidence: Both repair paths are measured: an arriving configuration entry restores the full set while the node is still a member, and an installed snapshot restores it when log replication is impossible, so a cluster with membership traffic, snapshots or a lagging node closes the gap without operator action.
Snapshot configuration is loaded correctly by restoreSnapshot, so the gap needs a committed configuration entry between the last snapshot (or index 0) and the recovered commit index.
No captured test asserts configuration state after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, so the captured suite neither contradicts nor covers this path.
limitations: Applies to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.
All measurements use the repository's in-memory transport, commit-tracking store and mock FSM; monotonic store variants and production stores are not measured.

The installed-snapshot repair needed the leader's log to have been compacted past the node's last index, which the probe arranged by letting the cluster commit eighty entries while the node was down; other ways of reaching that state are not measured.
interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts of the same harness file answer this question. Two state the gap itself (5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 and e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9, each at its own indices 0 and 1). Two state the repair paths separately: 183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f at indices 15 and 16 for an arriving configuration entry, and 5627b36f50384d14851e4b5da991fa96 at indices 30 and 31 for an installed snapshot after the leader's log had been compacted past the node's last index.
